sub: Database design, functional dependencies and normal forms
why: Armstrong's augmentation axiom for functional dependencies (a -> b implies ya -> yb). Functional dependency inference rules sit in this leaf.
Equivalence rules for query transformation are the algebraic rewriting step of query optimisation.
Transmission delay = packet length / transmission rate is a data-communications performance formula. Not web architecture; the 2026 syllabus contains no networking unit.
OSI/TCP-IP layer terminology (segments vs datagrams vs frames). Pure data communications, not HTTP/DNS/client-server web architecture.
NetWare protocol stack (IPX/SPX/NCP/NetBIOS) mapped onto OSI layers. Legacy LAN networking; no unit of TECH1 or TECH2 covers OSI layer protocols.
The four P's of software project management (People, Product, Process, Project). Software project management was dropped entirely from the 2026 syllabus.
Prototyping process model from software engineering / systems analysis. No TECH1 or TECH2 unit covers SDLC process models.

sub: Concurrency control, locking and time stamping
why: Compares timestamp ordering against two-phase locking on conflict serializability and deadlock freedom - exactly this leaf.
ACID properties are the defining guarantees of a database transaction.
Unshielded twisted pair is a transmission medium - data communications cabling. Nothing in the 2026 syllabus covers transmission media.
IPv4 classful addressing (identifying a Class C address). Networking address arithmetic, explicitly outside the web-architecture leaf.
Definition trivia about what constitutes a computer network. General networking fundamentals, not covered by any 2026 unit.
Software design principles from software engineering (design quality). The 2026 syllabus dropped software engineering entirely.
UML diagrams and DFDs used to build a system analysis model. Systems analysis and design / software engineering modelling, absent from the 2026 syllabus.
Waterfall SDLC process model. Software engineering process models are not in TECH1 or TECH2.

sub: Data models and the relational model: keys, tuples, domains and relational algebra
why: Tuple vs domain relational calculus - the formal query languages of the relational model. The leaf names tuples, domains and relational algebra; relational calculus is taught alongside them. Slight stretch since 'calculus' is not spelled out.
